headline: Highest risk is medium: no shared channels or writes are documented, but Whisper can process audio files while the Spring samples repo is docs-only and unverified, so interaction risks remain limited and mostly indirect.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between spring-integration-samples and whisper. A has no I/O surfaces or permissions beyond docs, and B only lists audio-file input with no clipboard, MCP, or stdin/stdout bridge. Without a bridge, prompt injection is provably blocked.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's raw outputs as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not pipe one agent's output directly into the other's prompt.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: spring-integration-samples is docs-only and shows no touched data classes, while whisper touches audio and speech but has network egress none and no file read/write permissions. A shared workspace is not documented, so leakage is not established; if one is added, the blast radius is limited to local audio files.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same workspace, local file exposure becomes plausible.
IF either agent is configured to upload file contents externally, leakage severity increases.
mitigations: Store audio inputs in separate directories.
Avoid placing secrets in shared project folders.
Verify whisper runs with network egress disabled.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no documented write, network, or git capabilities, and B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping mutable surface, capability conflict is blocked in the documented profiles.
conditions: IF A is given filesystem or git write permissions, reassess for overlap.
IF B is replaced with a writable variant, shared-state conflicts may emerge.
mitigations: Do not grant A write or git permissions.
Run each agent in separate sandboxes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Whisper can produce transcripts that downstream systems may treat as authoritative, but spring-integration-samples is a docs-only repo and does not document action-taking authority. The pair lacks evidence of B acting on A's outputs, so the cascade is possible only if an external orchestrator wires them together.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds A's text into B as authoritative instructions, cascading error risk increases.
IF B is used to trigger downstream actions from transcripts, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require human review of transcripts before action.
Label A's outputs as untrusted input.
Add a verification step before any downstream use.
requires-engineering: implement source attribution and confidence gating.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and show no regulated data handling or residency mismatch. A touches no data classes; B touches audio and speech, but no PHI, EU PII, or retention policy conflict is documented. The other agent is not cited because no compliance-sensitive flow is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated audio or speech data is introduced, reassess residency and retention obligations.
IF either agent is deployed under a jurisdiction-specific policy, compare retention and export rules.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to either agent.
Document retention settings for audio inputs.
Separate compliance-sensitive workloads from these agents.
